\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভূমিকম্প} (bhūmikômpô)}{ভূমিকম্প (bhūmikômpô)}]{\bn{ভূমিকম্প} (bhūmikômpô) — an earthquake}

\label{lesson:BN-C293-bhumikompo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to crack, then the Bengali for to be scorched.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভূমিকম্প}}
\textbf{\bn{ভূমিকম্প}} — \emph{bhūmikômpô} — \textquotedblleft{}an earthquake\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ভূমিকম্পে} \bn{শহরের} \bn{অনেক} \bn{পুরনো} \bn{বাড়ি} \bn{ভেঙে} \bn{পড়ল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhūmikômpe shôhôrer ônek purôno bāṛi bhenge pôṛlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many old buildings in the city collapsed in the earthquake.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভূমিকম্প}} (\emph{bhūmikômpô}) is Sanskrit \emph{bhūmikampa}, 'an earthquake' (Monier-Williams): \emph{bhūmi}, 'the earth', and \emph{kampa}, 'trembling'. In the example, \bn{ভেঙে} carries \bn{ঙ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūmikômpô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūmikômpô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūmikômpe shôhôrer ônek purôno bāṛi bhenge pôṛlô.} — Many old buildings in the city collapsed in the earthquake.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to crack, then the Bengali for to be scorched, then say \emph{bhūmikômpô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ভূমিকম্প} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An earthquake\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কম্পন} (kômpôn)}{কম্পন (kômpôn)}]{\bn{কম্পন} (kômpôn) — a tremor; a shaking}

\label{lesson:BN-C293-kompon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to be scorched, then the Bengali for an earthquake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কম্পন}}
\textbf{\bn{কম্পন}} — \emph{kômpôn} — \textquotedblleft{}a tremor; a shaking\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{প্রথমে} \bn{একটা} \bn{ছোট} \bn{কম্পন} \bn{হল}, \bn{তারপর} \bn{একটা} \bn{বড়} \bn{কম্পন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{prôthôme ekṭā chhoṭo kômpôn hôlô, tārpôr ekṭā bôṛo kômpôn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
First there was a small tremor, then a big one.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কম্পন}} (\emph{kômpôn}) is Sanskrit \emph{kampana}, 'trembling, shaking' (Monier-Williams), the noun beside \emph{kampa} in \textbf{\bn{ভূমিকম্প}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kômpôn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kômpôn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôthôme ekṭā chhoṭo kômpôn hôlô, tārpôr ekṭā bôṛo kômpôn.} — First there was a small tremor, then a big one.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to be scorched, then the Bengali for an earthquake, then say \emph{kômpôn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কম্পন} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A tremor; a shaking\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়া} (dhôse pôṛā)}{ধসে পড়া (dhôse pôṛā)}]{\bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়া} (dhôse pôṛā) — to cave in; to collapse}

\label{lesson:BN-C293-dhose-pora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an earthquake, then the Bengali for a tremor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়া}}
\textbf{\bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়া}} — \emph{dhôse pôṛā} — \textquotedblleft{}to cave in; to collapse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ভূমিকম্পে} \bn{পাহাড়ের} \bn{রাস্তা} \bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়ল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhūmikômpe pāhāṛer rāstā dhôse pôṛlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mountain road caved in during the earthquake.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{দেয়াল} \bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়ল}, \emph{sei deyāl dhôse pôṛlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়া}} (\emph{dhôse pôṛā}) is the -e form of \bn{ধসা}, to fall in — Sanskrit \emph{dhvaṁsati}, 'falls to pieces' (CDIAL 6896, which lists Bengali \emph{dhasā}) — before \bn{পড়া}, to fall.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhôse pôṛā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūmikômpe pāhāṛer rāstā dhôse pôṛlô.} — The mountain road caved in during the earthquake.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an earthquake, then the Bengali for a tremor, then say \emph{dhôse pôṛā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ধ্বংস} (dhvôngsô)}{ধ্বংস (dhvôngsô)}]{\bn{ধ্বংস} (dhvôngsô) — destruction; ruin}

\label{lesson:BN-C293-dhvongso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a tremor, then the Bengali for to collapse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ধ্বংস}}
\textbf{\bn{ধ্বংস}} — \emph{dhvôngsô} — \textquotedblleft{}destruction; ruin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ভূমিকম্পে} \bn{পুরো} \bn{শহরটা} \bn{ধ্বংস} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhūmikômpe puro shôhôrṭā dhvôngsô hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The whole city was destroyed in the earthquake.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ধ্বংস}} (\emph{dhvôngsô}) is Sanskrit \emph{dhvaṃsa}, 'a falling down, ruin' (Monier-Williams), the learned noun beside \textbf{\bn{ধসে} \bn{পড়া}}, which wore the same root down to \bn{ধস}. \bn{ধ্বংস} \bn{হওয়া}, to be destroyed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhvôngsô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhvôngsô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūmikômpe puro shôhôrṭā dhvôngsô hôlô.} — The whole city was destroyed in the earthquake.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a tremor, then the Bengali for to collapse, then say \emph{dhvôngsô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ধ্বংস} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Destruction; ruin\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{চাপা} \bn{পড়া} (chāpā pôṛā)}{চাপা পড়া (chāpā pôṛā)}]{\bn{চাপা} \bn{পড়া} (chāpā pôṛā) — to be trapped underneath; to be buried under}

\label{lesson:BN-C293-chapa-pora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to collapse, then the Bengali for destruction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{চাপা} \bn{পড়া}}
\textbf{\bn{চাপা} \bn{পড়া}} — \emph{chāpā pôṛā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be trapped underneath; to be buried under\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ভাঙা} \bn{বাড়ির} \bn{নিচে} \bn{কিছু} \bn{মানুষ} \bn{চাপা} \bn{পড়ল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhāngā bāṛir niche kichhu mānush chāpā pôṛlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Some people were trapped under the collapsed house.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{লোক} \bn{দেয়ালের} \bn{নিচে} \bn{চাপা} \bn{পড়ল}, \emph{sei lok deyāler niche chāpā pôṛlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{চাপা} \bn{পড়া}} (\emph{chāpā pôṛā}) puts \bn{চাপা}, 'pressed down' — CDIAL 4674, a Middle Indo-Aryan \emph{capp-}, which lists Bengali \emph{cāpā}, 'to press' — before \bn{পড়া}: to fall under a weight.
\end{cousinweb}
